nodes.content: Design a multi-tenant storage engine that isolates write latency while sharing compaction capacity and preserving crash-consistent tenant boundaries.
requirements: Keep tenant p99 write latency within 2× its standalone baseline during competing compactions within quotas.
Prevent cross-tenant data exposure and storage quota evasion across crashes and capacity reassignment.

nodes.content: Reserve per-tenant write I/O; token-schedule compaction; atomically journal quota-charged, tenant-encrypted SST ownership and generation-fenced capacity reassignment.
How should compaction tokens yield to reserved write I/O when two tenants saturate the same SSD?
Under competing compactions, per-tenant write I/O reservations and 4-ms preemptible compaction slices keep write p99 ≤2× standalone.
Run DualTenant-SSD with two quota-compliant writers and competing compactions; compare reserved-I/O write p99 against standalone using 4-ms slices.
DualTenant-SSD: 4-ms slices kept worst-tenant write p99 at 5.4 ms versus 3.2 ms standalone (1.69×).
Adopt reserved write I/O with 4-ms compaction slices; DualTenant-SSD's 1.69× worst-tenant p99 meets the 2× target.
After adopting reserved write I/O and 4-ms slices, implement atomic ownership/quota journaling, tenant encryption, and crash-reassignment tests.
Implement tenant-encrypted SSTs and atomic OwnerLedger WAL records binding owner, charged bytes, and capacity generation before publication.
OwnerLedger v1 adds tenant-encrypted SSTs and atomic WAL records for owner, charged bytes, and capacity generation; recovery rejects stale files.
Run OwnerLedger v1 CrashReassign-1000 power cuts and capacity transfers under competing compactions; check write p99, cross-tenant reads, quota charges.
CrashReassign-1000 found 7/1,000 crashes left uncharged compaction temp SSTs after capacity reassignment, allowing tenant storage quota evasion.
Retain reserved write I/O and 4-ms compaction slices; durably precharge encrypted SSTs to tenants and reconcile orphans before reassignment.
Compaction inputs identify one tenant and yield a conservative temporary-byte bound before allocation, enabling quota-safe precharges across crashes.
Trace OwnerLedger v1 on MixedSST-10k, checking input-owner uniqueness and preallocation byte bounds against peak temporary allocation.
MixedSST-10k found 83/10,000 compactions with inputs from two tenants, invalidating single-tenant precharges.
Tenant-partitioned outputs with durable precharges prevent mixed-owner compaction quota evasion across crashes while maintaining write p99 ≤2× standalone.
Prototype tenant-partitioned outputs and durable precharges atop OwnerLedger v1; run mixed-owner CrashReassign-1000 and DualTenant-SSD, checking quotas, reads, and p99.
DualTenant-SSD measured worst-tenant write p99 at 7.1 ms versus 3.2 ms standalone (2.22×); precharge fsyncs stalled writes.
Batch durable precharges before compaction allocation on a reserved metadata I/O lane; rerun DualTenant-SSD and CrashReassign-1000 atop OwnerLedger v1.
Batched precharges yielded 5.8-ms write p99 versus 3.2-ms standalone (1.81×); CrashReassign-1000 found zero uncharged bytes or cross-tenant reads.
Batch tenant-partitioned encrypted-SST precharges before allocation on reserved metadata I/O; expect zero quota leaks, cross-tenant reads, and write p99 ≤2×.
Integrate batched precharges into OwnerLedger v1; run reassignment CrashReassign-100k and DualTenant-SSD, checking quota leakage, cross-tenant reads, write p99.
CrashReassign-100k found zero uncharged bytes or cross-tenant reads; DualTenant-SSD write p99 was 5.9 ms versus 3.2 ms (1.84×).
Combine epoch-fenced capacity reassignment, batched tenant-specific precharges, encrypted SSTs, reserved write I/O, and 4-ms compaction slices.
How are in-flight compaction outputs fenced when their tenant’s capacity generation changes during reassignment?
Generation-checked publication rejects stale SSTs; retaining tenant precharges until durable deletion prevents reassignment leaks and cross-tenant reads.
Run FenceRace-10k: reassign after output fsync but before publication; crash before deletion; inspect stale-output rejection, charges, and cross-tenant reads.
FenceRace-10k found 4/10,000 crashes refunded precharges before stale SST deletion became durable, leaving uncharged bytes after reassignment.
Retain reserved-write scheduling and encrypted SSTs; quarantine stale-generation outputs, then fsync directory deletions before journaled refunds or capacity reassignment.
Implement quarantine-to-delete-before-refund ordering, gate reassignment on durable cleanup, then rerun FenceRace-10k and DualTenant-SSD.
Implement QuarantineLedger: block reassignment until stale SST unlink and directory fsync complete, then journal tenant refunds.
QuarantineLedger v2 gates capacity reassignment on durable stale-SST deletion and journals refunds afterward, preserving tenant charges until cleanup.
Run FenceRace-10k and DualTenant-SSD on QuarantineLedger v2; verify durable refunds, tenant isolation, reassignment safety, and write p99.
FenceRace-10k found zero uncharged bytes or cross-tenant reads; DualTenant-SSD write p99 was 6.0 ms versus 3.2 ms (1.88×).
Stress QuarantineLedger v2 with ChurnReassign-50k: overlap mixed-tenant compactions, power cuts, and repeated capacity transfers; audit quotas, isolation, write p99.
ChurnReassign-50k: cleanup fsync bursts raised quota-compliant tenant write p99 to 7.6 ms versus 3.2 ms standalone (2.38×).
Defer QuarantineLedger v2 deployment: FenceRace-10k validates isolation, but ChurnReassign-50k's 2.38× write p99 exceeds 2×; isolate cleanup fsyncs.
Batch stale-SST deletions per epoch; throttle directory fsyncs to spare SSD bandwidth and gate reassignment on durable cleanup.
How can cleanup fsync bursts be reduced without releasing capacity before stale SST deletions become durable?
With durable batched precharges, epoch-batched deletions and throttled directory fsyncs keep write p99 ≤2× standalone without premature refunds.
Implement epoch-batched deletes and throttled fsyncs atop OwnerLedger v1; rerun ChurnReassign-50k, auditing write p99, premature refunds, and cross-tenant reads.
ChurnReassign-50k yielded 5.9-ms write p99 versus 3.2-ms standalone (1.84×), with zero premature refunds or cross-tenant reads.
On OwnerLedger v1, run FsyncBoundary-100k power cuts across batched deletion and reassignment; verify charges, stale-file access, and write p99.
FsyncBoundary-100k found 3 crashes where refund journal commits preceded durable directory fsyncs, resurrecting uncharged stale SSTs.
Retain batched precharges; epoch-batch deletions, fsync directories before refunds or reassignment, and throttle cleanup for ≤2× write p99.
Enforce directory fsync before refunds and reassignment on OwnerLedger v1; rerun FsyncBoundary-100k and ChurnReassign-50k, auditing quotas and write p99.
FsyncBoundary-100k found zero resurrected uncharged SSTs; ChurnReassign-50k write p99 was 6.1 ms versus 3.2 ms (1.91×).
Adopt fsync-before-refund epoch batching: it fixes three crash leaks while maintaining 1.91× write p99, unlike the unsafe 1.84× variant.
Integrate throttled epoch deletions, directory fsync-before-refund, tenant encryption, and reserved write I/O; validate crash quotas and ≤2× p99.
Implement QuarantineLedger v3 with throttled epoch-batched deletions, directory fsync-before-refund, reassignment gating, and reserved metadata I/O.
QuarantineLedger v3 adds epoch-batched cleanup, fsync-before-refund ordering, generation-fenced reassignment, tenant-encrypted SSTs, and reserved write I/O.
Run CrashReassign-100k, FsyncBoundary-100k, ChurnReassign-50k, and DualTenant-SSD on QuarantineLedger v3; audit isolation, charges, and write p99.
QuarantineLedger v3: 250k crash/churn trials found zero uncharged bytes or cross-tenant reads; worst write p99 was 1.91× standalone.
Run EightTenant-Saturation at 90% SSD occupancy on QuarantineLedger v3; audit refunds, cross-tenant reads, and write p99 during reassignment.
EightTenant-Saturation at 90% occupancy reached 7.4-ms worst-tenant write p99 versus 3.2-ms matched standalone (2.31×).
At 90% occupancy, admit cleanup fsyncs only during write-queue slack; retain precharges until durable deletion to target ≤2× p99.
Using OwnerLedger v1’s journal, gate QuarantineLedger v3 cleanup fsyncs at write-queue depth ≤2; rerun EightTenant-Saturation and FsyncBoundary-100k.
EightTenant-Saturation write p99 fell to 5.9 ms versus 3.2 ms (1.84×); FsyncBoundary-100k found zero premature refunds.
Adopt write-queue-slack cleanup gating: crash-safe v3 met 1.91× p99, saturation reached 2.31×, and gating restored 1.84× without premature refunds.
Revise v3 to gate cleanup fsyncs at write-queue depth ≤2; preserve fsync-before-refund and retest eight-tenant saturation and crashes.
Implement QuarantineLedger v4 atop v3: gate cleanup directory fsyncs at write-queue depth ≤2; refund only after durable deletion.
QuarantineLedger v4 adds write-queue-slack cleanup gating to v3 while retaining fsync-before-refund, epoch-fenced reassignment, and tenant-encrypted SSTs.
Run EightTenant-Saturation, ChurnReassign-50k, and FsyncBoundary-100k on QuarantineLedger v4; check write p99, quota charges, and tenant reads.
QuarantineLedger v4: EightTenant-Saturation write p99 was 5.9 ms versus 3.2 ms (1.84×); 150k crash/churn trials found zero leaks.
Adopt QuarantineLedger v4: slack-gated cleanup cuts saturation p99 from v3’s 2.31× to 1.84×; 150k trials found zero isolation/quota failures.
